subject: space
title: Rotation & Revolution
name: Rotation & Revolution
tagline: Two completely different motions, happening at the same time
summary: Earth is always doing two things at once: spinning on its own axis (rotation), and gliding along its path around the Sun (revolution). They're easy to mix up because they're both called "Earth's motion" — but one takes about 24 hours and the other takes about 365 days, and you can change how fast either one happens without touching the other at all.

whyItMatters: Rotation is why every place on Earth gets a day and a night. Revolution is why a full year takes as long as it does. Confusing the two is one of the most common mix-ups in astronomy — and the fastest way to un-confuse them is to watch both happen at once, at speeds you control independently.
didYouKnow: The equator is moving faster than a commercial jet — about 1,670 km/h — just from Earth's rotation, even though it never feels like we're moving at all.
conditions: Earth spins on a fixed axis

compareReason: Rotation and revolution are the two raw motions; tilt is what turns revolution into seasons. Seeing plain revolution first (no tilt effect highlighted) makes it obvious what tilt actually adds.
